content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm currently working with [company_name] [product_name] [article_no], a switch [product_name] [article_no], and an HMI panel [product_name]. My goal is to connect these devices together. I am able to transfer programs between the [product_name] and my computer, and I can also upload the project to the HMI panel. However, when I attempt to change a tag on the HMI, I get a 'Value could not be written to PLC' error. I've followed available tutorials, but they haven't been helpful. The software I use only detects the HMI on the network. Any suggestions?
Your [product_name] appears to be the current [product_name] [version_no]. Have you enabled S7 access in the project properties? Are the HMI and [product_name] on the same IP subnet?
Yes, I believe everything is configured correctly. Please see my attachments.

At first glance, your setup seems fine. I would recommend changing the [product_name]'s device address to something other than 1, such as 3 or another value. I can't test this myself as I don't have the actual HMI panel on hand. From my tests with simulated HMIs, communication worked with [product_name] [version_no] versions prior to [version_no], but not with [version_no]. It's possible that new security features in [version_no] could be causing issues with HMI connections. If you're still stuck, it's a good idea to reach out to [company_name] support.
Hello, Which version of [product_name] engineering software are you using? Best regards, [user_name]

There are FAQs that cover similar applications, such as this one: [url] Although the example uses older versions, you can adapt the instructions for current hardware. You indicated that you define IP settings and enable S7 communication as well as connections in the HMI. However, it looks like you may have missed creating a server S7 connection in the [product_name]. See the FAQ for guidance.

No. When I set up a connection with earlier [product_name] [version_no] versions, I didn't need to create a server connection in the [product_name] program—just defining the connection in the HMI was sufficient.

Here's a video demonstrating a test with a simulated HMI and a [company_name] [product_name] [version_no]. There are delays on the HMI display, since I periodically powered off the [product_name] and the switch. This highlights that the connection is only established when both devices are powered on. The delays are mainly due to the switch requiring about 30 seconds to become operational.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing issues connecting a [company_name] PLC with an HMI via an industrial switch; attempts to modify tags on the HMI result in errors, and typical troubleshooting steps haven't resolved it. There is particular uncertainty around new security features in the latest [product_name] [version_no], which may be impacting HMI communications previously supported in older versions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward and reliable communication between the latest [company_name] PLC and HMI panels, including seamless read/write tag operations. They also look for up-to-date online documentation matching their hardware versions.
